title: Acceptance criteria: bounded resumable streams, retry budget, and schema-anchored tool handoffs
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Background: Customers integrating function/tool calls over streaming responses need predictable semantics for partial emissions, deterministic resume behavior after transient failures, and robust schema anchoring so downstream services can materialize tool invocations reliably. This ticket defines acceptance criteria for resumable streams, bounded retry budgets, and a schema-anchored handoff contract between the model's structured output and the tool invocation layer. The goal is to unblock engineering work on runtime checkpoints and Console observability while clarifying edge cases for tool idempotency and error modes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Resume token contract: Every streamed response that may include a tool call MUST optionally emit a base64 'resume_token' in the final frame of each stable checkpoint. Resume token semantics documented: token encodes (model_version, last_emitted_frame_index, schema_anchor_id, optional kvcache_offset). If a client presents the token within its next request, runtime must resume from the next frame index with no duplicated tool invocations.

2) Bounded retry budget: For any single logical request, the system allows at most two automated internal retries after transient transport or worker preemption errors. Retries MUST NOT re-emit a confirmed tool invocation; if a tool call was acknowledged in telemetry, system must treat retries as resumed continuation, not fresh calls.

3) Schema anchoring and handshake: Structured output frames that declare a tool invocation MUST include a 'schema_anchor_id' matching a documented schema version for that tool. Runtime rejects frames where declared anchor is unknown with a clear error frame (error_code 'SCHEMA_MISMATCH', human_message).

4) Deterministic idempotency header: Tool invocation envelopes include an 'invocation_id' derived from request-id + frame-index. Downstream tool gateways must see identical invocation_id for retried/resumed attempts and behave idempotently. Acceptance tests will verify no duplicate side-effects across retries.

5) Partial-output visibility: If the model emits structured objects in multiple frames (fragmented), each emitted fragment will include an incremental 'fragment_index' and 'total_expected' when known. Clients may assemble partial objects; runtime must expose 'partial=true' in streaming terminal events when final object not yet complete.

6) Graceful fallback for schema drift: If model emits a field not present in the anchored schema, runtime will surface a non-fatal warning frame (warning_code 'SCHEMA_EXTRA_FIELD') and attempt to include the unexpected field in a 'raw_payload' subfield so tools can opt-in to best-effort parsing. This behavior must be configurable per-customer via console knob.

7) Hard failures and rollback: If an unrecoverable formatting error occurs (malformed JSON frame that breaks parsing) runtime must abort the stream with error_code 'MALFORMED_FRAME' and NOT send any further frames. If a tool invocation was already emitted but not acknowledged, runtime must mark the invocation as 'unknown' and emit an audit event for operator investigation.

8) Observability and telemetry assurance: For every stream that includes tool invocation frames, the runtime MUST emit events for 'stream_started', 'checkpoint_emitted', 'tool_invoke_sent', 'tool_invoke_ack'/'tool_invoke_fail', and 'stream_resumed' if a resume_token is used. These events must include invocation_id and schema_anchor_id.

9) Latency SLOs for resume: Resume path (client sends resume_token) should reestablish a continuation within 200ms P50 and 800ms P95 under normal load for Hosted API; acceptance validation will run synthetic tests against these targets in the staging cluster.

10) Client-timeout semantics: If the client does not supply a resume_token and reconnects within 5 seconds, runtime MAY attempt best-effort continuation; beyond 5 seconds the runtime must treat the session as new and must not retry previously emitted tool invocations.

11) Backpressure handling: If downstream tool gateways respond with 429/503, runtime must buffer up to a configurable 'tool_buffer_limit' (default 8 pending invocations per request) and apply progressive backoff with jitter. If buffer limit exceeded, runtime must emit 'TOOL_OVERLOAD' warning frames and surface fallback policy (e.g., route to an alternative tool or emit a soft-degraded schema response).

12) Migration compatibility: When a schema_anchor_id is retired, runtime must continue to accept the retired anchor for 30 days in parse-only mode (no new guaranteed tool invocations). Acceptance tests will include a simulated schema deprecation to validate parse-only behavior.
test_plan: 1) End-to-end synthetic: Create a test harness that streams a 6-frame structured-object with tool invocation in frame 4; force worker preemption after frame 4 and verify resume_token allows client to reconnect and receive frames 5-6 without a duplicate tool invocation (validate via invocation_id).

2) Idempotency validation: Use a stubbed tool gateway that records side effects. Trigger two resume scenarios (network retry + client reconnect) and assert side-effects count == 1 for a single logical invocation.

3) Schema drift scenario: Emit unexpected fields in a test model binary and verify runtime emits SCHEMA_EXTRA_FIELD warnings and includes raw_payload. Confirm console knob toggles opt-in parsing behavior.
4) Malformed frame injection: Inject broken JSON in frame stream and assert runtime aborts with MALFORMED_FRAME and emits audit event with invocation_id if applicable.
5) Observability smoke: Validate required telemetry events are present and linked to the same invocation_id across stream lifecycle; validate fields schema_anchor_id and fragment_index are populated.
6) Latency bench: Run resume path load tests in staging across representative request sizes to verify P50/P95 resume latency SLOs for hosted tier.
7) Backpressure reaction: Simulate repeated 503s from tool gateway and assert runtime follows buffer limit then emits TOOL_OVERLOAD warning and triggers configured fallback route.
8) Deprecation window: Mark a schema_anchor_id as retired in the staging control plane and confirm parse-only acceptance for 30-day window behavior.
9) Security review checklist: Validate invocation_id derivation does not leak PII, confirm resume_token entropy and signing, verify tokens expire after configurable TTL.
telemetry: events: stream_started, checkpoint_emitted, stream_resumed, tool_invoke_sent, tool_invoke_ack, tool_invoke_fail, stream_aborted
fields: request_id, invocation_id, schema_anchor_id, fragment_index, resume_token_present, worker_id, host_region, error_code
alerts: high-rate MALFORMED_FRAME or TOOL_OVERLOAD per customer -> trigger oncall paging, create a dashboard for resume success ratio
rollback_criteria: If resume path causes duplicated side effects in >0.1% of requests over a 1-hour window or if malformed-frame abort rate increases by >10x baseline after release, revert runtime change and disable resume token emission by feature flag.
notes: Design trade-offs: chose explicit invocation_id to shift idempotency responsibility to tool gateways rather than runtime dedupe state (saves memory at scale).
Operational: will add a runtime feature flag to disable resume tokens per-customer until security review completes.
Follow-ups: evaluate checkpoint compression to reduce resume_token size; consider authenticated resume tokens (HMAC) for Private deployments.
